candidates.title: Tools Need Not Speak in Text: Latent Context Compression for Agents
candidates.citationVelocity: ~4 days old (submitted 2026-11-04); Semantic Scholar HTTP 429 on every attempt this round
candidates.institution: Tsinghua AI Agent Group, Tsinghua University
communitySignals: listed on HuggingFace Daily Papers; no additional reproduction repo found on Papers with Code trending this round
credibilityEvidence: Tables 1-2: token-consumption reduction 70.01%-90.5% and runtime reduction 24.45%-56.0% vs Vanilla across 4 web-search QA benchmarks (NQ, TriviaQA, 2Wiki, HotpotQA) x 2 model pairings (Qwen3.5-35B-A3B+4B, GLM-4.7-Flash+Z1-9B), compared against 3 named baselines (LongLLMLingua, LLMSummary, ICAE)
Table 3: EM/F1 improves over Vanilla in all 4 benchmarks for both model pairings, best EM/F1 among all 5 methods in 6 of 8 model-dataset settings, up to +133.64% EM on HotpotQA
Section 3.2 theoretical codebook-capacity analysis motivating continuous over discrete-token compression
code released at github.com/THU-Agent/Coca-cola
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: controlled comparison against 3 established baselines plus a no-compression control, consistent across 2 model families and 4 QA benchmarks with ablations and a case study; validated only in the web-search tool-use setting, not other tool types (code execution, API calls)
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: the claim (continuous latent compression cuts token/runtime cost while improving task performance for web-search agents) is directly supported by the released code and the multi-baseline, multi-model comparison
candidates.primaryLimitation: evaluated only on web-search QA agents; generalization to other tool types (code execution, structured API calls) not yet tested
candidates.presentationReason: method section cleanly separates the context-aware encoder, latent adapter, and Action-Preserving Training objective, with a theoretical motivation section preceding the architecture
candidates.reason: selected: first method to compress tool observations into continuous latent tokens rather than reconstructing text, with a 4-baseline comparison, 2 model families, released code, and consistent task-performance gains alongside the efficiency gains; forms the 'compress before it enters context' leg of today's resource-efficiency cluster

candidates.title: How Do AI Agents Waste Your Money?
candidates.citationVelocity: ~4 days old (submitted 2026-11-04); Semantic Scholar HTTP 429 on every attempt this round
candidates.institution: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, Northeastern University, UCLA (Kai-Wei Chang among corresponding authors), UT Austin
communitySignals: not found on HuggingFace Daily Papers or Papers with Code trending this round
credibilityEvidence: Table 1: removing 14-20% of prefix tokens preserves 81.7-91.3% solved rate on SWE-bench Verified across 3 intervention points, tested on Kimi-K3 trajectories

Table 2: energy-distance permutation test (p<0.05 threshold, 2000 permutations) shows marked-waste removal shifts the next-action distribution in only 3.0%/10.5% of turns on SWE-bench/MCP-Atlas vs 25.0%/37.9% when all prior reasoning is removed
Table 3 online-pruning: removing 41%/46% of reasoning changes solved rate by <1pp on SWE-bench Verified and by 2.7pp on MCP-Atlas, vs -16pp/-9pp when all reasoning is deleted
cross-model analysis: ~18% of output tokens flagged as waste on average across 6 frontier models, 4 benchmarks, 5 harnesses
code + labeled trajectories released at github.com/huiminzeng/How_Do_AI_Agents_Waste_Your_Money and huggingface.co/datasets/huiminz3/How_Do_AI_Agents_Waste_Your_Money
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: causal intervention validation (remove-and-resume, remove-and-resample, remove-online) rather than only post-hoc LLM-judge labeling, across 6 frontier models, 4-5 benchmarks and 5 harnesses; the waste-identification step itself still depends on an LLM-as-a-Judge whose own false-positive/negative rate is not independently audited
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: causal intervention experiments plus open-sourced code and data support the claim that the measured waste is genuinely removable without materially changing task outcomes
candidates.primaryLimitation: the LLM-as-a-Judge's accuracy at flagging 'removable' content is not independently audited; a systematic judge bias would propagate into all downstream waste statistics
candidates.presentationReason: defines four waste patterns (Restate, Duplicate-Fetch, Padding, Detour) with concrete examples before presenting the three-stage tracing/identifying/verifying pipeline and the intervention experiments
candidates.reason: selected (carried forward from 2026-11-07 watch/stronger-competitor with no new signal needed -- re-read in full today and found to clear the credibility bar on its own merits): first framework to causally validate the 'token waste' label via direct remove-and-rerun intervention rather than aggregate usage measurement alone; forms the 'diagnose waste that already exists' leg of today's resource-efficiency cluster, complementing Coca-Cola's 'compress before it enters context'

candidates.title: Decoupled Predictive Decision Making: A Shared Conditional Predictor for Agents
candidates.venue: arXiv preprint (not peer-reviewed; cs.AI); 16 pages, 7 figures, 11 tables, with appendices
candidates.citationVelocity: ~7 days old (submitted 2026-11-01); Semantic Scholar HTTP 429 on every attempt this round
candidates.institution: Stable AI (Tsinghua-founded startup, publisher of the open LimiX/LimiX-2 structured-data foundation model family) + Tsinghua University (Peng Cui among corresponding authors)
communitySignals: HuggingFace Daily Papers, 79 upvotes observed -- one of the strongest community signals seen in this series recently
credibilityEvidence: Table 1 / Fig 2-3: mean accuracy across 50 benchmarks (82 task configs, 5 categories) with Qwen3.5-27B rises from 78.80% (few-shot) to 84.92% (DPDM); still 82.33% vs 78.80% under identical histories and queries, isolating the gain from sheer evidence volume

Table 2 label-permutation ablation: DPDM 80.71% vs 50.13% after permuting historical targets on fixed inputs (6 tasks), vs 50.52% for a most-frequent-label-only rule, showing the gain comes from learned input-target relationships, not memorized label frequencies
Fig 6: imbalanced-history test on all 5 BIG-Bench Mistake tasks (7,032 query steps) raises mean balanced accuracy from 59.86% (few-shot) to 74.37% (DPDM), gains in 18 of 20 encoder-task pairs
on ToolPRMBench BFCL: absolute accuracy gain of 34.26pp over few-shot prompting at matched history budgets
candidates.evidenceMaturityReason: well-designed ablations (label permutation, identical-history controls, growing-history and imbalanced-history tests) isolate the mechanism from simple confounds across 4 semantic encoders; the 50-benchmark suite, task compilation, and scoring pipeline are entirely self-defined by the authors, and no public evaluation-code or benchmark-list repository was found at review time
reproducibilityEvidence: LimiX-2 model weights published at huggingface.co/stable-ai/LimiX-2
candidates.editorialConfidenceReason: the label-permutation and identical-history ablations rule out the two most obvious confounds (more examples, more context volume alone), supporting the claim that the architecture learns genuine input-target relationships rather than just benefiting from a bigger prompt
candidates.primaryLimitation: the 50-benchmark composition, history budgets, and scoring pipeline are entirely self-defined by the authors; no public evaluation code was found at review time, so the pipeline's details cannot be independently inspected
candidates.presentationReason: cleanly separates the semantic-encoding role from the conditional-prediction role with explicit equations (Sec 2.1-2.3), and labels each experiment by which confound it is isolating (Sec 3.2-3.5)
candidates.reason: selected: decouples 'understanding the problem' (language model) from 'learning from deployment history' (a frozen structured-data predictor) into two independently improvable components rather than overloading one LLM with both via few-shot prompting; strong community signal (79 HF upvotes) and rigorous confound-isolating ablations; forms the 'offload the decision itself' leg of today's resource-efficiency cluster, completing compress / diagnose / decide
